text:
maria: Hey team, hit a long-context memory growth / leak during 200k-token runs on mixed H100/A100 clusters. RSS climbs steadily until OOM after ~12m tokens. Repro command and minimal logs below. :worried:

aj: Can you paste the exact command and logs? Also which kernel selection config was in use?

maria: repro: `./tools/longctx_repro --model redwood-7b --seq 200000 --gpus h100,a100,rtx6000 --reuse-window 1024 --batch 8`

LOG SNIPPET:
----BEGIN----
KV_PAGER: page_table_entries=65536 free_list=120 allocated=65416 reuse_hits=242
KV_PAGER: evict_scan_passes=0 owner_ptr=0x7f8a3c stale_owner_flag=1
WORKER[4]: allocate_kv_page idx=65535 -> mapped_idx=0 (wrap)
MEMORY: RSS +3.2GB (10m tokens)
----END----

maria: Note the "mapped_idx=0 (wrap)" line — looks like page index wrapping when table resized and some owners become stale. Happens more often in hybrid runs.

aj: Interesting. Two quick thoughts: 1) page index masking might be using an old mask if table resized without full fence across threads; 2) reuse logic may retire pages but leave stale owner ids that cause eviction to skip reclaim. Can you run with `KV_PAGER_LOG=trace` for one short run?

maria: ran trace for 1M tokens, attached excerpt. Repro gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro-2117 (private). Excerpt: 
```
pager: try_reuse page=65535 owner=0x12 dead=true -> skip
pager: eviction_scan hit_count=0, scanned=4096
pager: remap page=0 owner=0x12 -> claimed by worker-7 (stale)
```
chris: Profiling results from perf run (cpu-side):
- a100: avg pagewalk 1.1us, eviction path negligible
- h100: avg pagewalk 4.8us, eviction scan stalls kernel selection thread, throughput drop ~6% when eviction spikes
- rtx6000: behaves like a100 for this repro

perf-bot: @maria @aj Kanary results: CL 1234 correlated with 5-7% throughput regression on h100 longctx; a100 nearly flat. Suspect AVX/PCI ordering + p2p differences. :eyes:

aj: My hypothesis: when table resizes we update mask (size-1) without ordering across workers; on GPUs with different peer visibility and DMA ordering (h100 pathfinder), stale mappings can be seen by worker that thinks page is free -> double-claim or skip-evict. Proposed fix: make owner update atomic with a CAS-based claim + memory_fence after table resize. Also adjust eviction to treat owner==STALE as reclaimable.

aj: patch sketch:
```
old = atomic_load(&page->owner);
if (old == STALE) {
  if (atomic_cmpxchg(&page->owner, STALE, my_pid) == STALE) {
    // we won the claim
    init_page_for(my_pid);
  } else {
    // someone else claimed it concurrently
  }
}
// ensure mask/fence ordering when swap table ptr
cpu_wmb();
```

maria: That CAS path looks promising. Does it add expensive contention on h100?

chris: Ran aj's CAS patch on a small canary: results: memory growth stable across 20M tokens on mixed run. Perf hit: ~2% on h100 in microbench (eviction-heavy synthetic), negligible on a100/rtx6000. Suggest enabling CAS only for hybrid-gpu jobs or when table resize frequency > threshold.

maria: Nice. Next steps: 1) @aj open PR with CAS + owner==STALE reclaim logic; 2) @chris add a canary config to longctx suite (h100 mixed); 3) add CI perf test to detect regression (perf-bot). Can we also add a runtime flag `kv.pager.hybrid_safe=true` to gate behavior? :rocket:

ci-bot: Created ticket INF-872, and CI job `longctx/hybrid-h100-a100` added to canary pipeline.

aj: I'll draft PR today. Will include a compile-time guard and runtime flag, and a telemetry counter for "cas_reclaims" and "stale_owner_skips".

maria: Also let's add a short-term mitigation: `--kv.reclaim-eager=true --reuse-window=0` for affected deployments until PR lands. That prevents memory growth but costs token throughput.

chris: One more note: kernel selection path picks different eviction kernels for h100 (prefers async copies). The CAS introduces a tiny spin. If that ends up hurting h100, we can try a per-arch optimized fast-path using atomic exch (less memory ordering) or a small MRU fast retry.

maria: Great. Thanks. Please ping when PR is up. :thumbsup:

aj: ping @maria PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/789 (draft) — tests attached.

maria: Reviewing now. If green on canary, let's roll to dedicated clusters next week. :shipit: "
